bull.b: TTM revenue growth of 43.5% and Q2 revenue growth of 228% show accelerating commercial scale. A larger customer base can support recurring robot, software, service and cross-sell revenue, strengthening the platform’s ability to compound if execution remains consistent.

Two consecutive quarters of positive gross margin, including Q2 gross profit of $0.7M versus a prior-year gross loss, indicate early improvement in economics. The reported 80% assembly-time reduction and service changes could make future growth more scalable, though the turnaround remains early.

The estimated $27M of renewals, bookings and awards across 109 contracts provides evidence of customer retention and demand. Recurring awards can improve revenue visibility and validate adoption among enterprise and public-sector buyers, supporting a more durable commercial base.

bear.b: Despite strong sales growth, TTM gross margin remains about -10% and net margin about -217%, while gross profit was negative in every period provided. This indicates the offering has not yet established durable positive unit economics, making sustained scaling dependent on further margin improvement.

TTM operating cash flow of -$41.6M and free cash flow of -$42.9M show that expansion currently consumes substantial cash. With only $8.2M cash at quarter-end and burn worsening versus 2025 annual levels, funding needs could remain material unless conversion improves.

Q2 operating expenses rose 156% to $13.8M while net loss widened to $14.1M, driven by R&D, headcount and integration costs. Unless new products and the acquisition generate sufficient high-margin revenue, this cost structure could keep operating leverage negative over the next several quarters.
